wording: sunlit polar terrain is terrain where the criterion's proponents do not claim ice. It is NOT a proven ice-free null: subsurface ice can be thermally stable outside PSRs. These are real-data comparisons, not false-positive rates.
psr_mask: LOLA LPSR_75S_120M_201608, nearest neighbour at each cell's interpolated position

discs.rule: square lattice in polar-stereographic x, y; each disc keeps its n_F2 signal cells nearest the centre; discs with fewer dropped

comparison.flag: THE REAL SUNLIT RATE DIFFERS FROM THE SIMULATION BY MORE THAN 3 MC SE PLUS THE WILSON HALF-WIDTH

mantel_haenszel_inside_vs_outside.exposure: inside PSR (shadowed) against outside (sunlit); mixed excluded

logistic_fires.fit: IRLS, SEs from the inverse Fisher information

pairwise_overlap.note: discs are formed by assigning each signal cell to its nearest lattice centre and keeping cells within one radius, so no cell can belong to two discs; checked on the cached sunlit and PSR cells by position

v20_gap.interpretation: The coefficient of model (a) is a TOTAL-effect estimate of shadow: it contains whatever shadow does to the discs' polarization. The coefficient after adjusting for median coherence (models (c) to (e)) is a DIRECT-effect estimate, the part of shadow not mediated by coherence; coherence is a depolarization measure on the axis the rule thresholds, so the adjustment removes by construction any effect of ice on polarization. Neither is a false-positive rate: sunlit terrain is not a proven ice-free null.

e.model: (c) + slant-range sample/100, geometry-file incidence, LOLA local incidence

e0.model: (a) + slant-range sample/100, geometry-file incidence, LOLA local incidence (geometry without coherence)

per_disc_geometry_source.slant_range_sample: the SLC column of each of the disc's cells (median)
per_disc_geometry_source.slant_range_and_incidence_geometry: bundle geometry file (Slant_Range, Incidence_Angle), tie-point grid interpolated to the cell
per_disc_geometry_source.lola_local_incidence: LDEM_80S_20M gradient over +-2 posts (80 m), look vector from the geometry file; see the module docstring
